questions.question: Acceleration is defined as:
options: The change in velocity divided by the time taken — a = Δv/Δt
The change in position divided by the time taken

questions.question: The car goes from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. Its acceleration is:
options: 2 m/s² in the direction of motion

questions.question: While the car cruises at a constant 20 m/s, its acceleration is:
options: Zero — the velocity is not changing

questions.question: Braking from 20 m/s to rest in 5 s gives an acceleration of:
options: −4 m/s² — the velocity loses 4 m/s every second

subtopics.title: The Position-Time Graph — Gradient Is Velocity

questions.question: The gradient of a position-time graph gives the:
A horizontal line on a position-time graph means the object is:
options: Stationary — position unchanged while time passes

questions.question: During the car's speeding-up phase, its position-time graph is:
options: An upward curve that steepens — each second covers more ground

questions.question: A straight line sloping downward on a position-time graph shows:
options: Constant velocity in the negative direction — moving back towards the reference point
An object at rest below the axis

subtopics.title: The Velocity-Time Graph — Gradient and Area, Both Paying

questions.question: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient and the area under the graph give, respectively:
The braking phase falls from 20 m/s to 0 in 5 s. The gradient of that segment is:
The displacement during the speeding-up phase (0 to 20 m/s over 10 s) is the area of a triangle:
The total displacement for the whole journey (100 m + 400 m + 50 m) is:

subtopics.title: Reading All Three Graphs Together, and the Classic Traps

questions.question: For the car's journey, the acceleration-time graph looks like:
options: A single horizontal line at 2 m/s²
Flat steps: 2 for 10 s, 0 for 20 s, −4 for 5 s

questions.question: The 'gradient down, area up' family links say that:
options: Gradients of position-time give velocity, and areas under velocity-time give displacement
All three graphs have the same shape

questions.question: A rising straight line on a VELOCITY-time graph means the object is:
options: Moving away from the start at constant speed
Speeding up — not 'moving away', which is the classic misreading

questions.question: On a velocity-time graph, an object at REST is shown by:
options: A horizontal line at any height
A line lying on the time axis itself

questions.question: In the needle picture, acceleration measures:
options: How fast the taxi is moving
How far the taxi has travelled
How fast the speedometer needle itself is moving

questions.question: 'Two metres per second, per second' means:
options: Every second, the velocity grows by another 2 m/s
The taxi covers 2 m every second
The taxi's top speed is 2 m/s
The needle completes 2 turns per second

questions.question: A resting needle at 20 m/s means:
options: Zero acceleration while moving fast — the speed is simply not changing

questions.question: Passengers are tipped forward during which phase?
options: The braking — the needle falling as velocity is lost
No phase — passengers never feel acceleration

questions.question: The taxi trip's velocity-time silhouette is:
On the silhouette, steepness represents:
options: Acceleration — the driver's foot on accelerator or brake

questions.question: The falling ramp at the end of the graph means the taxi:
options: Slowed while still moving forward — height is speed, not position

questions.question: The taxi would only be moving backwards if the velocity-time graph:

subtopics.title: The Area That Pays Out in Metres

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph equals the:
The cruising plateau, 20 m/s for 20 s, contributes an area of:
options: 400 m — the rectangle height times width

questions.question: The pull-away triangle is HALF of the full-speed rectangle because:
options: Triangles are always half of everything
Speeding up from rest, the taxi averaged only half its top speed
The examiner removes half for rounding

questions.question: The braking triangle, ½ × 5 s × 20 m/s, gives a stopping distance of:
